output:
To: kitbash-market/murmur-dialogue/reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: 4 stars - Lanternfolk would not exist without Murmur, but read this before buying

I have used Murmur since 2022, so I want to add something honest to these reviews. I am giving it four stars for what it has made possible, not because the current version is safe to install without warnings.

The first prototype of my game Lanternfolk was literally its ferryman scene, made in one weekend with Murmur in 2022. That was also when I quit my job at a mobile studio. I had an idea, almost no time, and no interest in building a dialogue system before I could find out whether the scene was any good. Murmur let me make it instead. Lanternfolk now has 412 dialogue nodes and uses Murmur's CSV export for nine languages. It is not an exaggeration to say the game would not exist without this plugin.

But if you are buying it today, you need to know what is broken.

Version 3.2.0 has a serious save-loading bug. In my project, Murmur variables reset to their defaults when loading a save made in 3.1.x. That meant the ferryman forgot the player had already paid him, among other things. This is not a cosmetic issue; it can break progression and saved games.

The workaround that fixed it for me was rolling back to 3.1.4:

1. Back up your project first.
2. Get the 3.1.4 release.
3. Replace the Murmur folder in your project's addons folder with the 3.1.4 version.
4. Keep a copy of 3.1.4 and do not update the project to 3.2.0.

After doing that, my old saves loaded correctly again. Another developer confirmed the same workaround in my forum thread. We are staying on 3.1.4 for Lanternfolk's launch.

Ines has stepped back, and 3.2 is the last version she plans to make. The listing is still up at $29, but you are not buying the same actively supported tool I bought. If you are starting a new project, test saving and loading thoroughly and understand that there is currently a known, unresolved bug in the version being sold.

I understand being angry about that. I do not understand the cruelty of the review accusing her of taking people's money and running. I paid $19 in 2022 and received four years of updates for a tool I could use in unlimited commercial projects. That was an absurdly good deal, and dismissing all of it because the final update is broken is not fair.

The source is now public under MIT, which means Murmur does not have to end here. Someone can fork it, fix the save issue, and carry it forward. I might even look at doing that myself after Lanternfolk launches, although I am not making any promises before then.

So: four stars, with a very real warning attached. Stay on 3.1.4 if it works for your project, and do not buy 3.2.0 blind.

Thank you, Ines, for making something I could learn in a weekend and then build an entire game on. Lanternfolk is part of what those four years of work made possible.
